analysis.subject: computing
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers purpose and voluntary nature of framework for trustworthy AI, collaborative development process, resource center and profiles for generative AI and critical infrastructure, plus prior documents and translations

overview.headline: Voluntary framework for managing trustworthy AI risks

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the framework is intended for voluntary use to improve trustworthiness across design, development, use, and evaluation.
keyPoints.quote: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) is intended for voluntary use and to improve the ability to incorporate trustworthiness considerations

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the framework helps manage risks to individuals, organizations, and society associated with artificial intelligence.
keyPoints.quote: framework to better manage risks to individuals, organizations, and society associated with artificial intelligence (AI)

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the framework was developed through a consensus-driven, open, transparent, and collaborative process including public input.
keyPoints.quote: developed through a consensus-driven, open, transparent, and collaborative process that included a Request for Information

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a generative AI profile helps organizations identify unique risks and proposes actions aligned to their goals.
keyPoints.quote: The profile can help organizations identify unique risks posed by generative AI and proposes actions for generative AI risk management

keyTerms.gloss: Ability to incorporate reliable behavior that supports trust in design and evaluation
keyTerms.quote: to improve the ability to incorporate trustworthiness considerations into the design, development, use, and evaluation

keyTerms.gloss: Systems that create new content and bring unique risks needing specific management actions
keyTerms.quote: unique risks posed by generative AI and proposes actions for generative AI risk management that best aligns

keyTerms.gloss: Systems and operators whose reliable function is vital and who consider specific risk practices
keyTerms.quote: AI RMF Profile on Trustworthy AI in Critical Infrastructure. The profile will guide critical infrastructure operators

keyTerms.gloss: Computer systems that perform tasks associated with intelligent behavior and carry societal risks
keyTerms.quote: framework to better manage risks to individuals, organizations, and society associated with artificial intelligence (AI)

keyTerms.gloss: Optional adoption intended to improve ability to add trustworthiness considerations
keyTerms.quote: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) is intended for voluntary use and to improve the ability to incorporate trustworthiness considerations

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Students place framework milestones in chronological order to see how collaborative development shaped the voluntary guidance over time
componentPlan.focusQuote: Released on January 26, 2023, the Framework was developed through a consensus-driven, open, transparent, and collaborative process

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Students recall core purposes and profiles of the framework through checkable facts that reinforce trustworthy AI practices
